WITH sex_counts AS (
  SELECT 
    p.SEX,
    COUNT(*) as count
  FROM Examination e
  JOIN Patient p ON e.ID = p.ID
  GROUP BY p.SEX
),
stats AS (
  SELECT 
    SUM(count) as total_count,
    COUNT(*) as num_groups
  FROM sex_counts
),
with_calcs AS (
  SELECT 
    sc.count,
    sc.count / CAST(s.total_count as REAL) as share,
    s.total_count / CAST(s.num_groups as REAL) as avg_count_per_sex,
    sc.count - (s.total_count / CAST(s.num_groups as REAL)) as excess
  FROM sex_counts sc
  CROSS JOIN stats s
),
above_avg AS (
  SELECT 
    count,
    share,
    excess
  FROM with_calcs
  WHERE count > avg_count_per_sex
)
SELECT 
  SUM(count) as total_count,
  AVG(share) as avg_share,
  AVG(excess) as avg_excess
FROM above_avg

assumptions.assumption: Per-sex average count is the arithmetic mean across all sex groups: total_count / number_of_sex_groups
Phrase 'count is above the average' uses strict inequality (>), not ≥

alternatives.interpretation: If 'above the average' includes equality (>=), include sex groups whose count equals the per-sex average
